purpose: Executed M0 host-compatibility evidence for jey-adapter-dsh: a real Cordis context running the published DSH agent loop, observed through Jey-shaped plugins.

commands.note: tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit over src/**/*.ts and test/**/*.ts, no suppressions
node --test "test/host/*.test.ts" -> tests 7, pass 7, fail 0, duration ~0.34s, fully offline
deliberate negative typecheck probe (scratch file, since deleted); it exited 2 with the diagnostics recorded under typeContractFindings

host.testkit: @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop-testkit, which mounts LlmRuntime, SessionStore, SessionProjectionRegistry, SystemPrompt, ToolRuntime, AgentRegistry and deliberately no LLM adapter

resolvedVersions.note: read from repo/node_modules/.pnpm after install; the 12 @deepseek-ai/* packages declared by packages/adapter-dsh are all 0.1.7-alpha.1, cordis is 4.0.3, but 9 transitively pulled leaf packages resolved to 0.1.7-alpha.2

versionSkew.detail: dsh-brand, dsh-ptc-runtime, dsh-sandbox, dsh-sandbox-policy, dsh-timeout, dsh-typert-protocol, dsh-user-approval, dsh-util-crypto, dsh-util-values resolved to 0.1.7-alpha.2 while the pinned core stayed 0.1.7-alpha.1
versionSkew.consequence: the probe ran against a mixed tree, not a pure 0.1.7-alpha.1 closure. It passed, so no observed behaviour depended on the skew, but this artifact does not certify 0.1.7-alpha.1 in isolation and any Jey lockfile claim must name the resolved set above.

observedSequenceNotes: one turn, two steps: step 1 is the scripted tool call, step 2 is the scripted text answer
the probe listener records 'pre-execute' on waterfall entry and 'pre-execute-decision' once the inner chain settles, so entry-time order is not polluted by the await
the monotonic guard stage fires after the whole tools/pre-execute waterfall has settled and before tools/execute, exactly as the source comment claims

assertions.test: observes assemble -> pre-step -> pre-execute -> execute -> result on the real runtime
checks: indexOf(assemble) < indexOf(pre-step) < indexOf(llm-request) < indexOf(pre-execute) < indexOf(execute) < indexOf(result)
the probe tool body ran exactly once with note 'probe-note-1'
the session log contains a turn/end event

assertions.test: advertises exactly the assembled tool set to the model
checks: two assemblies and two model requests
every assembly's advertised set equals its returned set equals ['jey_probe_note']
each request's GenerateOptions.tools equals that assembly's returned set by name

assertions.test: stops the tool body when a tools/pre-execute listener denies the call
checks: probe tool body call list is empty
the chain decision observed by the probe is 'deny'
no 'execute' stage was observed
the single durable tool/result text is exactly 'Error: probe-policy-denied'

assertions.test: lets a monotonic guard denial outrank a waterfall allow
checks: a later-registered waterfall listener returned {kind:'allow'} and the probe observed decision 'allow'
indexOf(guard) > indexOf(pre-execute)
probe tool body call list is empty and no 'execute' stage was observed
the durable tool/result text matches 'Error: jey-probe-guard-denied'

assertions.test: gives tools/result observers a frozen outcome and no return channel
checks: Object.isFrozen(exec), Object.isFrozen(result) and Object.isFrozen(result.content) are all true
both mutation attempts from a second tools/result observer threw TypeError ('result:TypeError', 'result.content:TypeError')
the model-visible durable result is still 'probe-note-1', unchanged by the observer

assertions.test: degrades an ask decision to a denial because no approval service is composed
checks: a listener returning {kind:'ask', reason:'probe-ask'} was observed as decision 'ask'
the tool body never ran and no 'execute' stage was observed
the durable tool/result text is exactly 'Error: probe-ask', i.e. the ask degraded to a denial carrying its own reason

assertions.test: reports frozen parsed arguments to pre-execute listeners
checks: exactly one pre-execute observation for 'jey_probe_note'
Object.isFrozen(exec.arguments) is true
the frozen arguments round-trip to {"note":"probe-note-1"}

claims.claim: system-prompt/assemble runs before agent/pre-step, so a restriction made inside pre-step cannot affect the request already assembled for that step
claims.reason: assertion A-01 observed assemble at trace index 0 and pre-step at index 1 on the real loop for both steps; the ordering is host behaviour, not a source reading

claims.claim: the model-visible tool set exists only in PromptAssembly.tools and reaches the adapter from there
claims.reason: A-02: every assembly's returned tool-name set equalled the tools array of the immediately following real model request; LlmCallConfig carries no tools field

claims.claim: a tools/pre-execute waterfall listener returning {kind:'deny'} prevents the tool body from running
claims.reason: A-03: body call list empty, no tools/execute stage, and the denial reason is what the model read back

claims.claim: a synchronous ctx.tools.guard() denial cannot be overridden by a waterfall listener that allows
claims.reason: A-04: the waterfall decision observed by the probe was 'allow', yet the guard ran afterwards, the body never executed, and the call surfaced as an error carrying the guard reason

claims.claim: tools/result is an emit: the outcome is deep-frozen and observers have no return channel
claims.reason: A-05 froze nothing by policy — the host had already frozen exec, result and result.content; mutation threw TypeError and the model-visible content was unaffected. Independently, the published signature returns undefined and the negative typecheck probe reports TS2322 for an observer returning a value

claims.claim: parsed tool arguments cross the pipeline frozen and lossless
claims.reason: A-07: Object.isFrozen(exec.arguments) true at tools/pre-execute, JSON round-trip equal to the scripted call

claims.claim: an ask decision can be granted through this harness
claims.reason: the registry resolves ask through ctx.get('approval'); with no ApprovalService composed it degrades to denial (proven by A-06). Granting needs @deepseek-ai/dsh-user-approval, which is not a declared dependency of packages/adapter-dsh and whose service also insists on an open turn for its approval/asked + approval/decided audit pair. No approval-granted PASS is claimed

claims.claim: ctx.tools.restrict() is a scope filter that requires agent.ctx and throws on a global ctx
claims.reason: not exercised in this probe run: the probe plugins register global listeners and the guard marker only; no assertion was executed, so no PASS is recorded here

claims.claim: a Jey-shaped plugin (name/inject/apply) loads into a real DSH context and sees the extension points it declares
claims.reason: probe-plugin (inject: ['tools']) and scripted-llm (inject: ['llm']) were loaded with ctx.plugin() and every declared listener fired, including cross-service ones (system-prompt/assemble and agent/pre-step fired from a fiber that injects only tools)

claims.claim: the pinned 0.1.7-alpha.1 core installs and runs on this machine offline
claims.reason: typecheck clean and 7/7 tests green on Node v24.15.0 with no network and no API keys; see versionSkew for the alpha.2 leaf caveat

typeContractFindings.finding: the design brief's `import { create } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'` does not exist; tsc reports TS2339 "Property 'create' does not exist on type 'typeof import(...cordis/lib/types/index)'". The real entry point is the exported class: new Context()
typeContractFindings.impact: adapter construction and any ADR text must say new Context(); no factory import

typeContractFindings.finding: ctx.on() is typed per event: a listener whose return disagrees with Events[name] fails with TS2322 even when written inline (probes: {kind:'nope'} at tools/pre-execute, a number-returning tools/result listener). The untyped fallback overload on EventsService did not swallow either case
typeContractFindings.impact: listener signature drift is a build failure in this package, so Jey policies can rely on the compile-time contract

typeContractFindings.finding: tools/result is declared to return undefined, so 'the return value is ignored' is enforced by the type, not merely by the dispatcher; the immutability half of the claim is enforced by a deep freeze the host applies before observers run
typeContractFindings.impact: a Jey presentation layer cannot reshape a result from tools/result; it must act in tools/post-execute

typeContractFindings.finding: no type mismatch was found between the recorded HOST_CONTRACT signatures and the installed 0.1.7-alpha.1 .d.ts files for the events this probe uses; the ctx.on listener types resolved through Scoped<...> accepted plain arrow functions
typeContractFindings.impact: docs/HOST_CONTRACT.md section 3 stays authoritative for these five extension points

limitations: one scripted provider route ('jey-probe') and one registered tool; provider selection, retry, and PTC presentation are untested
the probe observes ordering and decisions from global listeners; agent-scoped (Scoped<Agent>) dispatch filtering and ctx.tools.restrict() are not exercised
ask approval grant path unreachable offline without dsh-user-approval; only its documented degrade-to-deny is proven
evidence was produced against a mixed 0.1.7-alpha.1 / alpha.2 tree (see versionSkew)
